title: Trump-Kim summit bid failed over North Korean conditions: Wall Street Journal report
html:
US President Donald Trump and North Korea leader Kim Jong Un last met in person in 2019.

PHOTO: AFP

US President Donald Trump explored the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his recent Asia tour, but the summit failed to materialise after Pyongyang presented conditions Washington deemed unacceptable, the Wall Street Journal (WSJ) reported on Nov 21.

The details of the conditions set by North Korea remain unknown.

Trump, whose political standing has weakened following his Republican Party’s defeat in the midterm elections earlier in November, sought a legacy-defining diplomatic achievement, but efforts to arrange the summit reached an impasse, said WSJ.

Before departing for his overseas trip, Trump told reporters that he might meet Kim in China. The WSJ said Trump had strongly urged his aides to arrange a meeting with Kim, whom he last met in person in 2019.

Trump visited the Philippines for Association of Southeast Asian Nations-related meetings and China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit earlier.

US officials considered formally ending the 1950-1953 Korean War, whose fighting ceased under an armistice agreement more than 70 years ago, WSJ said. The officials were alsocited as discussing the issuance of a statement that would neither recognise North Korea as a nuclear-armed state nor demand dismantlement of its nuclear programme, it added.

In return, Washington planned to seek limits on North Korea’s nuclear tests and missile launches, the WSJ said, adding that the US may have pursued establishing a liaison office as a first step towards diplomatic relations.

Trump, who met Kim three times in 2018 and 2019 during his first term, tried to reach Kim in 2025 through existing telephone lines and communication channels but received no response, the newspaper said. He then wrote a letter that US officials delivered to a North Korean diplomat outside the country’s mission to the United Nations in New York.

The letter, however, was reportedly returned unopened to a US representative at a UN meeting. KYODO NEWS
summary: The details of the conditions set by North Korea remain unknown.
